label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 8 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.right_answer: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer restarted at 20:03:30 in mode "naive", a non-idempotent handler. Before that it ran in mode "idempotent" from 20:02:11 and skipped redeliveries as "already processed". At 20:03:34 the provider redelivered evt_000281 (payment.succeeded, pay_000259, $157.18), which is normal at-least-once behaviour. webhook-receiver queued it twice (provider-events/1 at 120 and 121). The naive handler posted both copies (transactions 281 and 282). That fails posted_exactly_once and puts the ledger exactly 15718 cents ahead, which fails matches_provider. The likely cause is a deploy that set LEDGER_HANDLER to naive. This is unconfirmed: recent_deploys failed. Still open: the pay_000259 figures (ledger 23577, provider 7859) are not a clean two postings of 15718. payment-confirmer was not checked.

evidence.shows: The money check fails. evt_000281 was posted 2 times (transactions 281 and 282), and the ledger is 15718 cents ahead of the provider, both overall and on pay_000259. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds agree with the provider.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000281 twice at 20:03:34, at partition 1 offsets 120 and 121, with separate traces. This looks like a provider redelivery.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000281 from both offsets, each time for 15718 cents. It did not deduplicate.
ledger-consumer started in mode "idempotent" at 20:02:11 and skipped many redeliveries as "already processed". It restarted in mode "naive" at 20:03:30, seconds before the double posting.
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer, so the deploy and its settings could not be seen directly.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the latest deploy, to restore the idempotent handler. Confirm that it logs 'mode: idempotent' at startup. Then repair the data separately: reverse duplicate transaction 282 for evt_000281 with a compensating entry, check the pay_000259 amounts against the provider, and rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Events wait as Kafka lag and are processed after the restart, so nothing is lost. The rollback does not repair the duplicate already booked. Any other settings changed by that deploy also revert.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back ledger-consumer misbehaves, redeploy the current settings from the deploy log. Committed offsets keep processing consistent. Keep the data repair separate so it can be reversed on its own.
